name: Lorn Stark
age: 44 — grey at the temples only, brown elsewhere; reads as solid mid-40s, not old
body: broad, heavy Stark frame built bigger and heavier than his sister Fern's; a soldier's build that is durable and competent rather than impressive — never a gifted swordsman, but trained every day for years, so the frame reads as sturdy labor rather than athletic flash
texture: faint gravel from age and outdoor soldiering, not a growl
energy: low-key, steady, never raised; the authority sits in the flatness, not in volume
register: plain-spoken military direct address — no flourish, no filler, no wasted syllables; reports and gives instructions rather than persuades; goes silent or physical (a handclasp, not a speech) at the one moment emotion actually threatens the flatness

evidence.source: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Lorn Stark — The Sword-Teacher.md, section 'Voice'
evidence.quote: Stark-direct. No wasted syllables, no wasted steps. He speaks the way he fights: competently, without flair, each word placed where the word serves the sentence's purpose and nowhere else. He does not raise his voice. He does not need to.

evidence.source: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Lorn Stark — The Sword-Teacher.md, section 'Physical Description'
evidence.quote: His body is the body of a man who was never exceptional with a blade and who trained every day regardless, producing a frame that is competent and durable rather than impressive

evidence.source: wiki/Volume I — Character Cards/Lorn Stark — The Sword-Teacher.md, section 'Physical Description'
evidence.quote: Forty-four and showing the specific accelerated grey that the last eleven years produced. Hair grey at the temples, brown elsewhere, cut in the northern military style.
"That is the third one of those," Lorn said. "And they do not agree."
Lorn found that the thing he wanted to say would not come out in any arrangement that was not embarrassing, so he put his hand out instead

reference_direction: Male, medium-low pitch, sitting a couple of semitones below neutral without going into deep-bass territory. Texture is plain and lightly weathered — a little dry gravel from age and years outdoors, not the raspy growl register (that belongs to Darius/Gimbzo, and Lorn is a different kind of man). Measured, unhurried pace with short, flat, declarative sentences and no rhetorical lift at the ends of lines — he reports and instructs, he doesn't perform. Minimal breathiness; the control is the point. No regional caricature — think a plain northern-frontier soldier's cadence, the voice of a career non-commissioned officer giving a status report, not a general rallying troops. One comparison: the flat, competent voice of a long-serving drill instructor who has never needed to shout to be obeyed.
one_line: A plain, medium-low, lightly weathered soldier's voice — flat, unhurried, and short-sentenced, with the emotion pushed down into a handclasp instead of a raised voice; archive gives him exactly one line, so the card's own 'Voice' section (Stark-direct, no wasted syllables, never needs to raise it) is doing most of the casting work here.
